text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kasim Begic, the Bosnian Moslem member of the election commission sponsored by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), resigned last week in protest against OSCE mission chief's decision to repeat local elections in divided town of Mostar, diplomatic sources say.
- Local elections in Mostar should not be repeated but the results of legal elections last June should be thoroughly implemented, says Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA).

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka, denies Croatian media allegations that Bosnian Croats cannot obtain Bosnian passports and that, by doing this, Bosnian authorities are blocking the Dayton peace agreement.
- Johanes Bamer, president of Austria Airlines, donates 250,000 Austrian schillings (35,000 German marks) for reconstruction of a hospital in Sarajevo.
- Bosnian trade union asks international High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, to name those guilty for delaying the international reconstruction donors conference.

- Moslem-Croat federation government offers proposal for privatisation of socially-owned flats. Apartments would sell for 600 German marks per square meter (three square feet) and could be paid in credits of up to 25 years. Various exemptions should reduce price to some 120 to 180 marks per square metre.

- Roman Catholic Bishop of southwestern Mostar-Duvno region, Ratko Peric, says Catholics from his region will come to Sarajevo for this week's visit of Pope John Paul II after city authorities assured him they had undertaken extensive security measures.
- Selim Beslagic, mayor of northern town of Tuzla and a member of an opposition party, denies that opposition Joint List coalition is disintegrating.

- Those who spit on streets, throw rubbish from their windows, throw flammable things into bins or dig through garbage containers will be fined from 100 to 500 German marks, Sarajevo county authorities say. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
